cna.title: slip: reject VJ receive packets on instances with no rstate array

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

slip: reject VJ receive packets on instances with no rstate array

slhc_init() accepts rslots == 0 as a valid configuration, with the
documented meaning of 'no receive compression'. In that case the
allocation loop in slhc_init() is skipped, so comp->rstate stays
NULL and comp->rslot_limit stays 0 (from the kzalloc of struct
slcompress).

The receive helpers do not defend against that configuration.
slhc_uncompress() dereferences comp->rstate[x] when the VJ header
carries an explicit connection ID, and slhc_remember() later assigns
cs = &comp->rstate[...] after only comparing the packet's slot number
to comp->rslot_limit. Because rslot_limit is 0, slot 0 passes the
range check, and the code dereferences a NULL rstate.

The configuration is reachable in-tree through PPP. PPPIOCSMAXCID
stores its argument in a signed int, and (val >> 16) uses arithmetic
shift. Passing 0xffff0000 therefore sign-extends to -1, so val2 + 1
is 0 and ppp_generic.c ends up calling slhc_init(0, 1). Because
/dev/ppp open is gated by ns_capable(CAP_NET_ADMIN), the whole path
is reachable from an unprivileged user namespace. Once the malformed
VJ state is installed, any inbound VJ-compressed or VJ-uncompressed
frame that selects slot 0 crashes the kernel in softirq context:

 Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical
       address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
 KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007]
 RIP: 0010:slhc_uncompress (drivers/net/slip/slhc.c:519)
 Call Trace:
  <TASK>
  ppp_receive_nonmp_frame (drivers/net/ppp/ppp_generic.c:2466)
  ppp_input (drivers/net/ppp/ppp_generic.c:2359)
  ppp_async_process (drivers/net/ppp/ppp_async.c:492)
  tasklet_action_common (kernel/softirq.c:926)
  handle_softirqs (kernel/softirq.c:623)
  run_ksoftirqd (kernel/softirq.c:1055)
  smpboot_thread_fn (kernel/smpboot.c:160)
  kthread (kernel/kthread.c:436)
  ret_from_fork (arch/x86/kernel/process.c:164)
  </TASK>

Reject the receive side on such instances instead of touching rstate.
slhc_uncompress() falls through to its existing 'bad' label, which
bumps sls_i_error and enters the toss state. slhc_remember() mirrors
that with an explicit sls_i_error increment followed by slhc_toss();
the sls_i_runt counter is not used here because a missing rstate is
an internal configuration state, not a runt packet.

The transmit path is unaffected: the only in-tree caller that picks
rslots from userspace (ppp_generic.c) still supplies tslots >= 1, and
slip.c always calls slhc_init(16, 16), so comp->tstate remains valid
and slhc_compress() continues to work.

cna.title: Open WebUI: SSRF Bypass via HTTP Redirect Following in Web-Fetch and Image-Load Endpoints

descriptions.value: Open WebUI is a self-hosted artificial intelligence platform designed to operate entirely offline. Prior to 0.9.5, the validate_url() function in backend/open_webui/retrieval/web/utils.py only validates the initial URL submitted by the caller. The HTTP clients used downstream (sync requests, async aiohttp, langchain's WebBaseLoader) follow HTTP 3xx redirects by default and do not re-validate the redirect target against the private-IP / metadata-IP block list. Any authenticated user can therefore submit a public URL that 302-redirects to an internal address (e.g. 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, RFC1918) and read the internal response body via the /api/v1/retrieval/process/web endpoint, the /api/v1/images/... endpoints, the /api/chat/completions endpoint with an image_url content part, and any other route that calls these helpers. cna.title: rxrpc: Fix potential UAF after skb_unshare() failure

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rxrpc: Fix potential UAF after skb_unshare() failure

If skb_unshare() fails to unshare a packet due to allocation failure in
rxrpc_input_packet(), the skb pointer in the parent (rxrpc_io_thread())
will be NULL'd out.  This will likely cause the call to
trace_rxrpc_rx_done() to oops.

Fix this by moving the unsharing down to where rxrpc_input_call_event()
calls rxrpc_input_call_packet().  There are a number of places prior to
that where we ignore DATA packets for a variety of reasons (such as the
call already being complete) for which an unshare is then avoided.

And with that, rxrpc_input_packet() doesn't need to take a pointer to the
pointer to the packet, so change that to just a pointer.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/iwcm: Fix workqueue list corruption by removing work_list

The commit e1168f0 ("RDMA/iwcm: Simplify cm_event_handler()")
changed the work submission logic to unconditionally call
queue_work() with the expectation that queue_work() would
have no effect if work was already pending. The problem is
that a free list of struct iwcm_work is used (for which
struct work_struct is embedded), so each call to queue_work()
is basically unique and therefore does indeed queue the work.

This causes a problem in the work handler which walks the work_list
until it's empty to process entries. This means that a single
run of the work handler could process item N+1 and release it
back to the free list while the actual workqueue entry is still
queued. It could then get reused (INIT_WORK...) and lead to
list corruption in the workqueue logic.

Fix this by just removing the work_list. The workqueue already
does this for us.

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The vulnerable cm_event_handler is driven by iWARP connection-management events generated from a remote peer's iWARP/MPA-over-TCP traffic (connect-request/reply/disconnect), delivered by the provider driver; an iWARP endpoint is reachable over a routed network, not just the local LAN.
AC:L - The attacker controls both the rate and pattern of connection events, so flooding connection requests at a listening cm_id reliably creates the multiple-events/reused-work-element condition (the bug reproduced readily under ucmatose stress); the attacker drives both sides of the race.
PR:N - Connection-request events are processed by the iwcm before any application-level authentication, so an unauthenticated remote peer that can speak iWARP/MPA to a listening endpoint needs no privileges on the target.
UI:N - Triggering requires only that the attacker initiate connection traffic; no action by a local user or victim is needed.
S:U - The corruption is confined to the kernel's own workqueue structures within the same security authority; no VM/IOMMU/sandbox boundary is crossed.
C:H - The bug is a use-after-free-class reuse of an iwcm_work element (whose contents include remote-supplied MPA private_data) causing workqueue list corruption, which per kernel scoring guidance can be leveraged for arbitrary memory disclosure.
I:H - Reinitializing a still-queued work_struct corrupts the workqueue's doubly-linked lists, giving a list-unlink write primitive over kernel memory that can be steered toward arbitrary write / control-flow hijack.
A:H - The corruption produces an immediate kernel BUG/Oops in the iw_cm_wq kworker (panic), and the underlying memory corruption can crash the system repeatedly.

descriptions.value:
A cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in Apache ECharts in the Lines series tooltip rendering logic.




This issue affects Apache ECharts: from before 6.1.0.

In versions prior to 6.1.0, if both Lines series and tooltip are used, and no user-specified tooltip.formatter is provided, and series.data[i].name is specified, raw HTML string series.data[i].name can be rendered through innerHTML sink into tooltip content. Although tooltip is allowed to accept user-provided raw HTML via a custom tooltip.formatter, the built-in tooltip formatters conventionally perform HTML escaping automatically. This case breaks that convention and may unexpectedly lead to script execution when tooltips are displayed.


Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.1.0 if using the Lines series in this way, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: s390/cio: Fix device lifecycle handling in css_alloc_subchannel()

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/cio: Fix device lifecycle handling in css_alloc_subchannel()

`css_alloc_subchannel()` calls `device_initialize()` before setting up
the DMA masks. If `dma_set_coherent_mask()` or `dma_set_mask()` fails,
the error path frees the subchannel structure directly, bypassing
the device model reference counting.

Once `device_initialize()` has been called, the embedded struct device
must be released via `put_device()`, allowing the release callback to
free the container structure.

Fix the error path by dropping the initial device reference with
`put_device()` instead of calling `kfree()` directly.

This ensures correct device lifetime handling and avoids potential
use-after-free or double-free issues.

The function that produces this secret, get_shared_secret() in crates/ecstore/src/rpc/http_auth.rs, falls back to the public, source-tree-embedded DEFAULT_SECRET_KEY = "rustfsadmin" when neither the RUSTFS_RPC_SECRET environment variable nor the global S3 secret key has been configured. cna.title: Roxy-WI: Authenticated arbitrary file write on every managed load balancer (and downstream RCE) via WAF rule save `config_file_name`

descriptions.value: Roxy-WI is a web interface for managing Haproxy, Nginx, Apache and Keepalived servers. In versions 8.2.6.4 and prior, POST /waf/<service>/<server_ip>/rule/<rule_id>/save accepts a config_file_name form field that is passed straight through to config_mod.master_slave_upload_and_restart(...) as the destination path. The validation chain (_replace_config_path_to_correct → check_is_conf) only requires the path to contain a hard-coded service substring (nginx/haproxy/apache2/httpd/keepalived) and the substring conf or cfg, and to not contain ... The encoded-slash substitution 92 → / is applied before the substring check, so the attacker can build any absolute path anywhere on the LB filesystem as long as it satisfies those substring constraints. The body of the WAF rule (config form field) is written verbatim to that path. By choosing a filename like 92etc92cron.d92nginx_cfg_evil (resolving to /etc/cron.d/nginx_cfg_evil), an attacker drops a cron entry on the load balancer with attacker-controlled content. Cron parses the file on its next scan, executing the embedded job as root — full RCE on every load balancer the caller's group manages. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches.

cna.title: rxrpc: Fix re-decryption of RESPONSE packets

scenarios.value:
AV:N - rxrpc is a UDP/IP network protocol; the vulnerable CHALLENGE/RESPONSE handling processes packets received from a remote peer (a connecting client, or a malicious/spoofed AFS server) over the network.
AC:L - The bug is gated on a transient `-ENOMEM`/`-EAGAIN` during handshake processing, but an attacker can induce the required memory pressure by flooding the target with concurrent rxrpc handshakes, making the failing `GFP_NOFS` allocation reachable repeatably.
PR:N - The CHALLENGE/RESPONSE packets are processed during the security handshake before the connection is secured (`RXRPC_CONN_SERVICE_CHALLENGING`), so no authentication or credentials are needed to reach the code.
UI:N - A server processing an incoming RESPONSE, and automated AFS clients/daemons processing a CHALLENGE, require no human interaction to trigger the fault.
S:U - The corruption and its impact are confined to the kernel's own memory/security authority; no crossing of a VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary is involved.
C:H - The CHALLENGE-path refcount underflow frees the `rxrpc_connection` while still referenced; a UAF lets an attacker reallocate and read controlled freed-object contents, enabling kernel memory disclosure.
I:H - The same use-after-free / refcount-underflow on the connection object enables heap grooming and write primitives over the freed structure, allowing kernel memory/control-flow corruption.
A:H - The double-put UAF and the re-decryption of partially-decrypted RESPONSE packets reliably oops/panic the kernel and abort connections, causing a denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rxrpc: Fix re-decryption of RESPONSE packets

If a RESPONSE packet gets a temporary failure during processing, it may end
up in a partially decrypted state - and then get requeued for a retry.

Fix this by just discarding the packet; we will send another CHALLENGE
packet and thereby elicit a further response.  Similarly, discard an
incoming CHALLENGE packet if we get an error whilst generating a RESPONSE;
the server will send another CHALLENGE.

cna.title: Rocket.Chat: Pre-Auth NoSQL Injection in OAuth2 Token Endpoint leading to Arbitrary User ATO

descriptions.value: Rocket.Chat is an open-source, secure, fully customizable communications platform. Prior to 8.5.0, 8.4.1, 8.3.3, 8.2.3, 8.1.4, 8.0.5, 7.13.7, and 7.10.11, an unauthenticated network attacker obtains a valid Rocket.Chat OAuth access token for an arbitrary user by sending a single HTTP POST with MongoDB query operators to /oauth/token. The Rocket.Chat OAuth2 server does not validate that grant parameters are strings before forwarding them to findOne({...}) against the oauth_apps and oauth_access_tokens collections, so an attacker substitutes {"$ne": null} for client_id, client_secret, and refresh_token and receives a freshly minted {access_token, refresh_token} pair bound to whichever user's refresh token Mongo returned first. The resulting access token is a first-class bearer credential against the full /api/v1/* surface as that user. By iterating with $nin / $regex operators the attacker walks the entire oauth_access_tokens collection, collecting one fresh access token per user per request. If any matched token belongs to an admin, the stolen bearer gives full admin API access (including Apps-Engine app installation, i.e. server-side code execution). No account, credentials, userId, or prior interaction with the instance are required. This vulnerability is fixed in 8.5.0, 8.4.1, 8.3.3, 8.2.3, 8.1.4, 8.0.5, 7.13.7, and 7.10.11.

descriptions.value: RustFS is a distributed object storage system built in Rust. Prior to 1.0.0-beta.2, improper validation in the PUT /rustfs/admin/v3/import-iam endpoint allows a user with ImportIAMAction to create service accounts under arbitrary parent identities, including the root user (minioadmin). The endpoint accepts attacker-controlled parent, claims, accessKey, and secretKey values without enforcing privilege boundaries or sanitization. This enables privilege escalation to full administrative access using a persistent, attacker-defined credential. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.0.0-beta.2.

cna.title: Heym < 0.0.21 Path Traversal File Upload via upload_file()

descriptions.value: Heym before 0.0.21 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the file upload endpoint that allows authenticated users to write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary locations by supplying a crafted filename with traversal sequences. Attackers can exploit the unvalidated filename parameter in the upload_file() handler to bypass path restrictions and write, read, or delete files outside the intended storage directory.

cna.title: Composer: Github Actions issued GITHUB_TOKEN disclosure in GitHub Actions logs

descriptions.value: Composer is a dependency Manager for the PHP language. Prior to 1.10.28, 2.2.28, and 2.9.8, Composer\IO\BaseIO::loadConfiguration() validates GitHub OAuth tokens with the regex ^[.A-Za-z0-9_]+$ and interpolates rejected tokens into an UnexpectedValueException; GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN values using the ghs_<id>_<base64url-JWT> format can contain -, fail validation, and be disclosed to stderr or CI logs. This issue is fixed in versions 1.10.28, 2.2.28, and 2.9.8.

cna.title: netfilter: nft_counter: serialize reset with spinlock

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nft_counter: serialize reset with spinlock

Add a global static spinlock to serialize counter fetch+reset
operations, preventing concurrent dump-and-reset from underrunning
values.

The lock is taken before fetching the total so that two parallel
resets cannot both read the same counter values and then both
subtract them.

A global lock is used for simplicity since resets are infrequent.
If this becomes a bottleneck, it can be replaced with a per-net
lock later.

cna.title: OpenSIPS: Denial of Service in watcherinfo XML generation from oversized watcher URI

descriptions.value: OpenSIPS is a Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) server implementation. Versions prior to 3.6.6 and 4.0.0-rc1 contain a denial of service vulnerability in the watcherinfo generation functionality. An attacker can create an oversized watcher entry by sending a SUBSCRIBE Event: presence request with a long From URI, and then trigger presence.winfo watcherinfo XML generation for the same presentity. OpenSIPS copies the stored watcher URI into a fixed-size stack buffer, overflowing it and crashing the process. A remote attacker can crash an OpenSIPS worker in deployments that expose handle_subscribe() and allow watcherinfo (presence.winfo) generation. The issue is configuration-dependent because the presence and presence_xml modules must be loaded and SUBSCRIBE routing must be reachable. This issue has been fixed in versions 3.6.6 and 4.0.0-rc1.

cna.title: Microsoft APM: Symlinks under `.apm/prompts/` and `.apm/agents/` are dereferenced during `apm install`, copying host-local file contents into the project tree

descriptions.description: CWE-59: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

descriptions.value: Microsoft APM is an open-source, community-driven dependency manager for AI agents. From 0.5.4 to 0.12.4, two primitive integrators in apm-cli enumerate package files with bare Path.glob() / Path.rglob() calls and read each match with Path.read_text(), transparently following symbolic links. A symlink committed inside a remote APM dependency under .apm/prompts/<x>.prompt.md or .apm/agents/<x>.agent.md is preserved verbatim into apm_modules/ on clone and then dereferenced during integration, with the resolved content written as a regular file into the project's deploy directories. The package content_hash, the pre-deploy SecurityGate scan, and apm audit do not flag this. The deploy roots are not added to the auto-generated .gitignore, so the resulting files are staged by git add by default. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.13.0.

cna.title: DIRAC: RCE in RequestManager due to eval on untrusted input

descriptions.value: DIRAC is an interware, meaning a software framework for distributed computing. Prior to versions 8.0.79, 9.0.22, and 9.1.10, the RequestManagementSystem/Service/ReqManagerHandler.py export_getRequestCountersWeb function passes an authenticated caller-controlled groupingAttribute to RequestManagementSystem/DB/RequestDB.py getRequestCountersWeb. An unrecognized value is resolved against the Request object and evaluated as Python code, allowing a crafted dunder attribute expression to reach operating-system functions and execute commands as the account running the DIRAC services. Successful exploitation can expose dirac.cfg, database passwords, stored proxies, and tokens, fully compromise the DIRAC system, and allow alteration of local log evidence. This issue is fixed in versions 8.0.79, 9.0.22, and 9.1.10.

On Windows, the missing directory resides in a location writable by any authenticated local user, enabling attackers to create the directory and place malicious files that execute at the privilege level of the user or service account that launches Konga, facilitating privilege escalation.

Prior to version 5.5.3 - #132, any authenticated user who can upload videos can add multiple subtitles from different files and change their title (English, Spanish...). The POST /actions/subtitle_edit.php request used to change their title includes a number parameter which is vulnerable to SQL Injection. cna.title: async-http-client: Cookie header not stripped on cross-origin redirect

descriptions.value: The AsyncHttpClient (AHC) library allows Java applications to easily execute HTTP requests and asynchronously process HTTP responses. Versions on the 2.x branch prior to 2.15.0 and the 3.x branch prior to 3.0.10 leak `Cookie` headers to cross-origin redirect targets. When following a redirect to a different origin, the `propagatedHeaders()` method in `Redirect30xInterceptor.java` strips `Authorization` and `Proxy-Authorization` headers but does not strip the `Cookie` header, causing session cookies and other sensitive cookie values to be sent to attacker-controlled servers. Versions 2.15.0 and 3.0.10 patch the issue.

descriptions.description: CWE-176: Improper Handling of Unicode Encoding

descriptions.value: FrankenPHP is a modern application server for PHP. From version 1.11.2 to before version 1.12.3, the splitPos() function in cgi.go misuses golang.org/x/text/search with search.IgnoreCase when the request path contains a non-ASCII byte. Two distinct flaws in that fallback let an attacker mislead FrankenPHP into treating a non-.php file as a .php script. In any deployment where the attacker can place content into a file served by FrankenPHP (uploads, file storage, etc.), this can be escalated to remote code execution by crafting a URL whose path triggers either flaw. This issue has been patched in version 1.12.3.

cna.title: ext4: drop extent cache after doing PARTIAL_VALID1 zeroout

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ext4: drop extent cache after doing PARTIAL_VALID1 zeroout

When splitting an unwritten extent in the middle and converting it to
initialized in ext4_split_extent() with the EXT4_EXT_MAY_ZEROOUT and
EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 flags set, it could leave a stale unwritten extent.

Assume we have an unwritten file and buffered write in the middle of it
without dioread_nolock enabled, it will allocate blocks as written
extent.

       0  A      B  N
       [UUUUUUUUUUUU] on-disk extent      U: unwritten extent
       [UUUUUUUUUUUU] extent status tree
       [--DDDDDDDD--]                     D: valid data
          |<-  ->| ----> this range needs to be initialized

ext4_split_extent() first try to split this extent at B with
EXT4_EXT_DATA_PARTIAL_VALID1 and EXT4_EXT_MAY_ZEROOUT flag set, but
ext4_split_extent_at() failed to split this extent due to temporary lack
of space. It zeroout B to N and leave the entire extent as unwritten.

       0  A      B  N
       [UUUUUUUUUUUU] on-disk extent
       [UUUUUUUUUUUU] extent status tree
       [--DDDDDDDDZZ]                     Z: zeroed data

ext4_split_extent() then try to split this extent at A with
EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 flag set. This time, it split successfully and
leave an written extent from A to N.

       0  A      B  N
       [UUWWWWWWWWWW] on-disk extent      W: written extent
       [UUUUUUUUUUUU] extent status tree
       [--DDDDDDDDZZ]

Finally ext4_map_create_blocks() only insert extent A to B to the extent
status tree, and leave an stale unwritten extent in the status tree.

       0  A      B  N
       [UUWWWWWWWWWW] on-disk extent      W: written extent
       [UUWWWWWWWWUU] extent status tree
       [--DDDDDDDDZZ]

Fix this issue by always cached extent status entry after zeroing out
the second part.

cna.title: LinkAce: IDOR in Update Policies Allows Any Authenticated User to Overwrite Other Users' Links, Lists, Tags, and Notes

descriptions.value: LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.5.6, LinkAce contains an Insecure Direct Object Reference vulnerability in the authorization policy layer that allows any authenticated user to modify resources owned by other users. The affected resource types are links, lists, tags, and notes. Both the web UI and the REST API are vulnerable. The root cause is in the update() methods of all four model policies: LinkPolicy, LinkListPolicy, TagPolicy, and NotePolicy. Each delegates to an access-check method (e.g., userCanAccessLink()) that returns true for any resource with non-private visibility, regardless of who owns it. This means any registered user can edit any public or internal resource across the entire instance. The delete() methods in the same policy files correctly require ownership via $link->user->is($user), which confirms that update was intended to be owner-only. The same flaw exists in the API layer through AuthorizesUserApiActions::userCanUpdateModel(), which mirrors the broken visibility-only check instead of the ownership check used by userCanDeleteModel(). Bulk edit operations via BulkEditController are also affected. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.5.6.

cna.title: Roxy-WI: LDAP injection in /user/ldap/<username> (admin-only)

descriptions.value: Roxy-WI is a web interface for managing Haproxy, Nginx, Apache and Keepalived servers. In versions 8.2.6.4 and prior, get_ldap_email (app/modules/roxywi/user.py:120-157) builds the LDAP search filter via f-string concatenation. The username URL path parameter is taken verbatim — no checkAjaxInput, no LDAP escape — and inserted, a username like *)(mail=*)(cn=* injects additional clauses, allowing the admin to enumerate or harvest attributes outside the intended record. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches.

cna.title: LiquidJS: Memory and render limit bypass via unbounded width padding in `date` filter (strftime)

descriptions.value: LiquidJS is a Shopify/GitHub Pages compatible template engine written in pure JavaScript. In versions 10.25.7 and below, the date filter's strftime implementation parses width specifiers like %9999999d and forwards the captured width unchecked into pad()/padStart(), leading to memory and render limit bypass. In src/util/underscore.ts, the pad loop performs unbounded string concatenation without consulting the Context's memoryLimit or renderLimit, so a single small template ({{ x | date: '%5000000d' }}) produces megabytes of output and unbounded CPU. The memoryLimit and renderLimit options the docs (src/liquid-options.ts:87-92) advertise as DoS controls — and which the docstring explicitly mentions for strftime — are entirely bypassed. Exploitation can cause large memory allocations, high CPU usage, or OOM crashes per render. This issue has been fixed in version 10.26.0.

When a user approves a task_create call (which requires ApprovalRequirement::Required), they approve what appears to be a benign work prompt. However, the spawned sub-agent silently receives unrestricted, unapproved shell access. This vulnerability is fixed in 0.8.26.

cna.title: cpuidle: Skip governor when only one idle state is available

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cpuidle: Skip governor when only one idle state is available

On certain platforms (PowerNV systems without a power-mgt DT node),
cpuidle may register only a single idle state. In cases where that
single state is a polling state (state 0), the ladder governor may
incorrectly treat state 1 as the first usable state and pass an
out-of-bounds index. This can lead to a NULL enter callback being
invoked, ultimately resulting in a system crash.

[   13.342636] cpuidle-powernv : Only Snooze is available
[   13.351854] Faulting instruction address: 0x00000000
[   13.376489] NIP [0000000000000000] 0x0
[   13.378351] LR  [c000000001e01974] cpuidle_enter_state+0x2c4/0x668

Fix this by adding a bail-out in cpuidle_select() that returns state 0
directly when state_count <= 1, bypassing the governor and keeping the
tick running.

cna.title: Heap-buffer-overflow write in planar bitmap decoder

descriptions.value: FreeRDP is a free implementation of the Remote Desktop Protocol. Prior to 3.26.0, FreeRDP's planar bitmap decoder has an out-of-bounds heap write when decoding RLE planar data. In libfreerdp/codec/planar.c, freerdp_bitmap_decompress_planar() validates the X destination coordinate nXDst against the caller-provided destination stride (nDstStep) even when it is writing into the internal temp buffer pTempData. An attacker can bypass the check with a large nDstStep and a large nXDst, causing planar_decompress_plane_rle() to write past the end of pTempData. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.26.0.

cna.title: DumbAssets 1.0.11 Path Traversal File Deletion via /api/delete-file

descriptions.value: DumbAssets through 1.0.11 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the POST /api/delete-file endpoint and filesToDelete array parameters that allows unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files by supplying ../ sequences that bypass directory boundary validation. cna.title: netfilter: nfnetlink_osf: fix divide-by-zero in OSF_WSS_MODULO

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nfnetlink_osf: fix divide-by-zero in OSF_WSS_MODULO

nf_osf_match_one() computes ctx->window % f->wss.val in the
OSF_WSS_MODULO branch with no guard for f->wss.val == 0. A
CAP_NET_ADMIN user can add such a fingerprint via nfnetlink; a
subsequent matching TCP SYN divides by zero and panics the kernel.

Reject the bogus fingerprint in nfnl_osf_add_callback() above the
per-option for-loop. f->wss is per-fingerprint, not per-option, so
the check must run regardless of f->opt_num (including 0). Also
reject wss.wc >= OSF_WSS_MAX; nf_osf_match_one() already treats that
as "should not happen".

Crash:

cna.title: netfilter: arp_tables: fix IEEE1394 ARP payload parsing

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: arp_tables: fix IEEE1394 ARP payload parsing

Weiming Shi says:

"arp_packet_match() unconditionally parses the ARP payload assuming two
hardware addresses are present (source and target). However,
IPv4-over-IEEE1394 ARP (RFC 2734) omits the target hardware address
field, and arp_hdr_len() already accounts for this by returning a
shorter length for ARPHRD_IEEE1394 devices.

As a result, on IEEE1394 interfaces arp_packet_match() advances past a
nonexistent target hardware address and reads the wrong bytes for both
the target device address comparison and the target IP address. This
causes arptables rules to match against garbage data, leading to
incorrect filtering decisions: packets that should be accepted may be
dropped and vice versa.

The ARP stack in net/ipv4/arp.c (arp_create and arp_process) already
handles this correctly by skipping the target hardware address for
ARPHRD_IEEE1394. Apply the same pattern to arp_packet_match()."

Mangle the original patch to always return 0 (no match) in case user
matches on the target hardware address which is never present in
IEEE1394.

Note that this returns 0 (no match) for either normal and inverse match
because matching in the target hardware address in ARPHRD_IEEE1394 has
never been supported by arptables. This is intentional, matching on the
target hardware address should never evaluate true for ARPHRD_IEEE1394.

Moreover, adjust arpt_mangle to drop the packet too as AI suggests:

In arpt_mangle, the logic assumes a standard ARP layout. Because
IEEE1394 (FireWire) omits the target hardware address, the linear
pointer arithmetic miscalculates the offset for the target IP address.
This causes mangling operations to write to the wrong location, leading
to packet corruption. To ensure safety, this patch drops packets
(NF_DROP) when mangling is requested for these fields on IEEE1394
devices, as the current implementation cannot correctly map the FireWire
ARP payload.

This omits both mangling target hardware and IP address. Even if IP
address mangling should be possible in IEEE1394, this would require
to adjust arpt_mangle offset calculation, which has never been
supported.

Based on patch from Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>.

cna.title: libp2p: Unvalidated PUT_VALUE records allow unbounded disk exhaustion on DHT server nodes

descriptions.value: libp2p is a JavaScript Implementation of libp2p networking stack. No credentials, no prior relationship, and no protocol deviation beyond a crafted key are required. The victim node's datastore fills until the host disk is exhausted, making the node unavailable. descriptions.value: Roxy-WI is a web interface for managing Haproxy, Nginx, Apache and Keepalived servers. In versions 8.2.6.4 and prior, ommit d4d10006 ("Expand validation to block .. in config_file_name and configver for improved security") added a line in app/modules/config/config.py:462. This is tuple-membership, not substring containment — '..' in (a, b, c) evaluates to True only if any of a, b, c is equal to the literal string '..'. cna.title: openvswitch: cap upcall PID array size and pre-size vport replies

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

openvswitch: cap upcall PID array size and pre-size vport replies

The vport netlink reply helpers allocate a fixed-size skb with
nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...) but serialize the full upcall PID
array via ovs_vport_get_upcall_portids().  Since
ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids() accepts any non-zero multiple of
sizeof(u32) with no upper bound, a CAP_NET_ADMIN user can install a PID
array large enough to overflow the reply buffer, causing nla_put() to
fail with -EMSGSIZE and hitting BUG_ON(err < 0).  On systems with
unprivileged user namespaces enabled (e.g., Ubuntu default), this is
reachable via unshare -Urn since OVS vport mutation operations use
GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM.

 kernel BUG at net/openvswitch/datapath.c:2414!
 Oops: invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 65 Comm: poc Not tainted 7.0.0-rc7-00195-geb216e422044 #1
 RIP: 0010:ovs_vport_cmd_set+0x34c/0x400
 Call Trace:
  <TASK>
  genl_family_rcv_msg_doit (net/netlink/genetlink.c:1116)
  genl_rcv_msg (net/netlink/genetlink.c:1194)
  netlink_rcv_skb (net/netlink/af_netlink.c:2550)
  genl_rcv (net/netlink/genetlink.c:1219)
  netlink_unicast (net/netlink/af_netlink.c:1344)
  netlink_sendmsg (net/netlink/af_netlink.c:1894)
  __sys_sendto (net/socket.c:2206)
  __x64_sys_sendto (net/socket.c:2209)
  do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63)
  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:130)
  </TASK>
 Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Reject attempts to set more PIDs than nr_cpu_ids in
ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids(), and pre-compute the worst-case reply
size in ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size() based on that bound, similar to the
existing ovs_dp_cmd_msg_size().  nr_cpu_ids matches the cap already
used by the per-CPU dispatch configuration on the datapath side
(ovs_dp_cmd_fill_info() serialises at most nr_cpu_ids PIDs), so the
two sides stay consistent.

cna.title: MyBooks: Privilege Escalation via Missing Authorization on Admin Settings Endpoint

Any authenticated regular user can therefore overwrite server configuration values including SMTP credentials, OAuth client secrets, storage paths, security feature flags, and autoreload settings. Exploitation can disclose secrets through configuration access paths, sabotage application behavior, force service restarts, and supply the settings needed for related code-injection attacks. cna.title: RDMA/rxe: Fix race condition in QP timer handlers

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The race is between the local rxe_destroy_qp verb and a local QP timer firing, both driven through the RDMA uverbs interface; a remote peer cannot create or destroy QPs, so local access is required.
AC:L - This is a race the attacker controls on both sides — creating a QP, driving RC traffic to arm the retransmit/rnr_nak timers, then destroying the QP — and it can be retried indefinitely across many QPs.
PR:L - Triggering requires issuing RDMA verbs (create/destroy QP, post sends) via the uverbs device, which in RDMA deployments is routinely granted to non-root users (rdma group / container device access).
UI:N - The attacker performs all QP creation, traffic, and destruction operations themselves with no victim action required.
S:U - The use-after-free is contained within the kernel's own security authority with no crossing of a VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary.
C:H - The refcount underflow / use-after-free on the QP object can give an attacker control over freed-object contents, enabling kernel memory disclosure.
I:H - A use-after-free of the QP object enables heap grooming and arbitrary write primitives, per kernel UAF scoring guidance.
A:H - The refcount underflow/use-after-free produces kernel warnings and can crash or panic the system when the freed QP is accessed.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/rxe: Fix race condition in QP timer handlers

I encontered the following warning:
 WARNING: drivers/infiniband/sw/rxe/rxe_task.c:249 at rxe_sched_task+0x1c8/0x238 [rdma_rxe], CPU#0: swapper/0/0
...
  libsha1 [last unloaded: ip6_udp_tunnel]
 CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/0 Tainted: G         C          6.19.0-rc5-64k-v8+ #37 PREEMPT
 Tainted: [C]=CRAP
 Hardware name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Rev 1.2
 Call trace:
  rxe_sched_task+0x1c8/0x238 [rdma_rxe] (P)
  retransmit_timer+0x130/0x188 [rdma_rxe]
  call_timer_fn+0x68/0x4d0
  __run_timers+0x630/0x888
...
 WARNING: drivers/infiniband/sw/rxe/rxe_task.c:38 at rxe_sched_task+0x1c0/0x238 [rdma_rxe], CPU#0: swapper/0/0
...
 WARNING: drivers/infiniband/sw/rxe/rxe_task.c:111 at do_work+0x488/0x5c8 [rdma_rxe], CPU#3: kworker/u17:4/93400
...
 refcount_t: underflow; use-after-free.
 WARNING: lib/refcount.c:28 at refcount_warn_saturate+0x138/0x1a0, CPU#3: kworker/u17:4/93400

The issue is caused by a race condition between retransmit_timer() and
rxe_destroy_qp, leading to the Queue Pair's (QP) reference count dropping
to zero during timer handler execution.

It seems this warning is harmless because rxe_qp_do_cleanup() will flush
all pending timers and requests.

Example of flow causing the issue:

CPU0                                   CPU1
retransmit_timer() {
    spin_lock_irqsave
                           rxe_destroy_qp()
                            __rxe_cleanup()
                              __rxe_put() // qp->ref_count decrease to 0
                            rxe_qp_do_cleanup() {
    if (qp->valid) {
        rxe_sched_task() {
            WARN_ON(rxe_read(task->qp) <= 0);
        }
    }
    spin_unlock_irqrestore
}
                              spin_lock_irqsave
                              qp->valid = 0
                              spin_unlock_irqrestore
                            }

Ensure the QP's reference count is maintained and its validity is checked
within the timer callbacks by adding calls to rxe_get(qp) and corresponding
rxe_put(qp) after use.

cna.title: @fastify/reply-from vulnerable to path traversal via backslash dot-segment prefix escape

descriptions.value: @fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions up to and including 12.8.0, the plugin validated proxy paths against forward-slash dot-segments only and then built the target with the WHATWG URL parser, which normalizes a backslash and its percent-encoded form to a forward slash on the http, https, ws, and wss schemes. A path that uses backslash dot-segments therefore bypasses the traversal check and resolves to a different upstream path, so an application that scopes proxying to an upstream prefix, or relies on route guards in front of the forwarding call, can have an unauthenticated request escape the intended prefix and reach other upstream endpoints. The resulting access to unintended upstream resources is primarily a confidentiality impact with limited integrity impact. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.1, where the path is normalized and any segment resolving to a single or double dot, along with control characters and ambiguous whitespace, is rejected before the URL is constructed, and users should upgrade to 12.8.1 or later. There is no workaround other than upgrading.

cna.title: Device-code claim permits restricted token escalation in Psono Server

descriptions.value: A restricted, short-lived API key session could be escalated to a full read-write session lasting up to 365 days, enabling unauthorized modification of encrypted secrets and shares.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Psono Server 7.2.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to Psono Server 7.2.4 or later.

descriptions.value: Psono Server versions 5.3.5 through 7.2.3 used a permission class that did not enforce token write scope when claiming a device code. An authenticated remote attacker holding a restricted API key-derived session could claim an attacker-controlled device code and obtain a full read-write session valid for up to 365 days, bypassing the original token's scope and lifetime restrictions. This did not bypass two-factor authentication or directly disclose plaintext secrets.

cna.title: File-transfer type confusion permits unauthorized repository writes in Psono Server

descriptions.value: A user with read-only file access could upload objects and append chunks in the file owner's external repository, affecting storage integrity and availability.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Psono Server 7.2.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to Psono Server 7.2.4 or later.

descriptions.value: Psono Server (CE & EE) versions 1.0.0 through 7.2.3 did not enforce the direction of file-transfer credentials on file-repository operations. An authenticated remote attacker with read-only access to a file could present a download transfer to the upload endpoint, obtain a signed upload URL for an attacker-selected object key, and append a chunk to the owner's file. Exploitation could upload or overwrite repository objects and consume storage, subject to transfer size, chunk-count, and lifetime limits.

cna.title: HTTP::Body versions before 1.24_01 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regex backtracking on the filename of a multipart upload

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Body 1.24_01 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.24_01 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regex backtracking on the filename of a multipart upload.

For every file part, the multipart parser finds the suffix of the uploaded filename by matching the default $basename_regexp, qr/[^.]+(\.[^\\\/]+)$/, against the whole basename. A basename made of many dots and ending in a backslash makes the regex backtrack in time quadratic in its length.

A remote attacker can exhaust CPU with one request, as a basename of about 32 KB takes several seconds to match and every file part is matched separately.

cna.title: Gitea Helm chart upload decompression denial of service

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #40085

descriptions.value: When parsing an uploaded Helm chart, Gitea decompressed the archive and read every tar entry while looking for `Chart.yaml` without limiting the decompressed size, and did so before the package size quota was checked; the quota only considers the compressed upload size. A user with package write access to an owner, for example their own account on an instance with open registration, could repeatedly upload small, highly compressed archives that make the server spend CPU time proportional to the decompressed size, degrading the availability of the Gitea instance. The issue does not allow code execution or data access.

cna.title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: jwt authorization grant bypasses identity provider login restrictions

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Hassan Akaou for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the JWT Authorization Grant implementation of the keycloak-services component. When an OIDC or Google identity provider is configured with specific login restrictions, such as claim filtering, these checks are correctly applied during standard browser logins but are skipped during the JWT-based grant flow. This allows an authenticated client to obtain access tokens for a user even if their identity provider claims should have blocked the login.

cna.title: Gitea public-only package token access to private OCI blobs

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #39853

descriptions.value: The OCI registry's cross-repository blob mount checked the target package against the token's `public-only` restriction, but checked the source blob only against the full account permissions of the token owner. A `public-only` token with `write:package` scope, whose owner can read a private package and write to a public package namespace, could mount a blob of the private package into the public package. cna.title: @fastify/session vulnerable to session revocation bypass via a logout race condition

descriptions.value: @fastify/session is a session plugin for Fastify. In all releases before 11.1.6, with the default rolling session behavior, a request that restored a session before a logout could save its own copy after another request had completed the session destroy call, recreating the destroyed session identifier with its authenticated data. An attacker who already holds a victim's valid signed session cookie and keeps a request in flight across the logout can replay that cookie to restore the session after it was meant to be revoked, without any cookie theft or signature forgery. The issue is fixed in @fastify/session 11.1.6, which adds a per session generation marker and a conditional store write so a session restored before a logout or regeneration cannot recreate or overwrite the current entry, and users should upgrade to 11.1.6 or later. There is no workaround, and custom session stores must implement the new conditional write.

cna.title: URL prefix handling permits API key read-scope bypass in Psono Server

descriptions.value: A write-only API key could read encrypted secret records through the bulk-secret-read endpoint despite having its read scope disabled.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Psono Server 7.2.4 or later.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to Psono Server 7.2.4 or later.

descriptions.value: Psono Server CE && EE versions 4.0.33 through 7.2.3 compared the request path for the bulk-secret-read endpoint with a hard-coded unprefixed path. In deployments configured with URL_PREFIX, the comparison failed and the POST request was authorized using write scope instead of read scope. An authenticated remote attacker with an unusual read-disabled, write-enabled API key could therefore retrieve encrypted secret data and nonces through the prefixed bulk-secret-read endpoint despite lacking read permission. The default configuration without URL_PREFIX was not affected.

cna.title: @fastify/multipart vulnerable to Denial of Service via a malformed upload hanging delayed file consumers

descriptions.value: @fastify/multipart is the multipart form-data and file upload plugin for the Fastify web framework. In versions 5.3.0 through 10.1.6, the plugin does not propagate a parser error to the file stream when a request body ends inside a file part with no closing boundary, even though the Content-Length is complete, the client does not abort, and no file size limit is exceeded. The plugin destroys the in-progress file stream without an error, so a handler that iterates the request parts and performs asynchronous work before consuming the file attaches to a stream that never emits an error or end event, and the request never responds while the connection stays open. An unauthenticated remote client can repeat these malformed uploads against such a route to accumulate pending connections and exhaust server resources, so the impact is availability only and exploitation depends on the application using a delayed file consumer. The issue is fixed in @fastify/multipart 10.1.7, where the parser error is propagated to the file stream so a delayed consumer settles with an error instead of hanging, and users should upgrade to 10.1.7 or later. There is no workaround other than upgrading.

cna.title: 389-ds-base: 389-ds-base: null pointer dereference via modifydn using an attribute's schema alias name causes denial of service

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Chad Sikorra for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Administrators should review custom access control instructions (ACIs) and avoid granting the ModifyDN (rename) right to non-administrative principals unless specifically required. Restricting this right reduces exposure to this issue until a fixed package is available. Neither 389-ds-base's own default ACI templates nor Red Hat Identity Management (IdM/FreeIPA)'s default ACIs grant this right to non-administrative users, so deployments that have not customized their ACIs are not exposed.

descriptions.value: A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in 389-ds-base. This flaw occurs when a ModifyDN (rename) operation uses an attribute's schema alias name (such as "commonName") instead of its canonical name (such as "cn") as the new relative distinguished name. An authenticated attacker with the ModifyDN (rename) permission on the affected entry can use this flaw to crash the directory server, causing a denial of service.

descriptions.value:
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_html allows an attacker who controls attribute names to inject attributes and script into rendered HTML via Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape/1.

attributes_escape/1 in lib/phoenix_html.ex escapes attribute values but not attribute names. key_escape/1 passes a binary key through html_escape, which neutralizes quotes and angle brackets but not whitespace, so a key such as x onmouseover ends the attribute and starts a new one. An atom key is only dasherized, so any character passes, including quotes and >. Nested data, aria and phx keys take the same paths. An application is affected when it builds attribute keys from untrusted input and renders them through HEEx <tag {@attrs}>, content_tag/3, or a direct call. Before 3.0.0 the same code lived in Phoenix.HTML.Tag.

This issue affects phoenix_html: from 1.0.0 before 3.3.5 and from 4.0.0 before 4.4.0.

* Install a vulnerable release, for example Mix.install([{:phoenix_html, "== 4.3.0"}]).
* Render a binary name containing a space: Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape(%{"x onmouseover" => "alert(1)"}) |> Phoenix.HTML.safe_to_string() returns  x onmouseover="alert(1)".
* Render an atom name containing a quote: Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape([{:"x\" onclick=\"alert(1)", "y"}]) |> Phoenix.HTML.safe_to_string() returns  x" onclick="alert(1)="y".

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Attribute rendering. Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape/1 walks the key-value pairs through build_attrs/1 and nested_attrs/3 and emits each as key_escape(k)="attr_escape(v)". Values are escaped. Names are not checked against the HTML attribute-name grammar.

2. Binary names. key_escape/1 sends a binary through Phoenix.HTML.Engine.html_escape/1, which replaces &, <, >, " and '. Whitespace passes. HTML uses whitespace to separate attributes, so %{"x onmouseover" => "alert(1)"} renders  x onmouseover="alert(1)": a harmless x attribute followed by an attacker-chosen event handler.

3. Atom names. key_escape/1 converts an atom with Atom.to_string/1 and replaces _ with -. Nothing is escaped, so [{:"x\" onclick=\"alert(1)", "y"}] renders  x" onclick="alert(1)="y" and aria: [{:"x\"><script>", "y"}] renders  aria-x"><script>="y", which leaves the tag entirely. This path needs the application to create atoms from untrusted input, for example Jason.decode!(body, keys: :atoms) or String.to_atom/1 on a parameter.

4. Reachability. HEEx compiles <div {@attrs}> to a call to Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape/1 through Phoenix.LiveView.HTMLEngine and Phoenix.LiveView.TagEngine. tag/2 and content_tag/3 in Phoenix.HTML.Tag (phoenix_html 1.x to 3.x) and in PhoenixHTMLHelpers.Tag (4.x) render attributes the same way. Versions before 3.0.0 emitted the dasherized name without any escaping at all.

**1. Attribute rendering.** `Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape/1` walks the key-value pairs through `build_attrs/1` and `nested_attrs/3` and emits each as `key_escape(k)="attr_escape(v)"`. Values are escaped. Names are not checked against the HTML attribute-name grammar.

**2. Binary names.** `key_escape/1` sends a binary through `Phoenix.HTML.Engine.html_escape/1`, which replaces `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`. Whitespace passes. HTML uses whitespace to separate attributes, so `%{"x onmouseover" => "alert(1)"}` renders ` x onmouseover="alert(1)"`: a harmless `x` attribute followed by an attacker-chosen event handler.

**3. Atom names.** `key_escape/1` converts an atom with `Atom.to_string/1` and replaces `_` with `-`. Nothing is escaped, so `[{:"x\" onclick=\"alert(1)", "y"}]` renders ` x" onclick="alert(1)="y"` and `aria: [{:"x\"><script>", "y"}]` renders ` aria-x"><script>="y"`, which leaves the tag entirely. This path needs the application to create atoms from untrusted input, for example `Jason.decode!(body, keys: :atoms)` or `String.to_atom/1` on a parameter.

**4. Reachability.** HEEx compiles `<div {@attrs}>` to a call to `Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape/1` through `Phoenix.LiveView.HTMLEngine` and `Phoenix.LiveView.TagEngine`. `tag/2` and `content_tag/3` in `Phoenix.HTML.Tag` (phoenix_html 1.x to 3.x) and in `PhoenixHTMLHelpers.Tag` (4.x) render attributes the same way. Versions before 3.0.0 emitted the dasherized name without any escaping at all.

cna.title: HTTP::Body versions before 1.24_01 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded buffering of chunked request bodies

solutions.value: Upgrade to HTTP-Body 1.24_01 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Body versions before 1.24_01 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded buffering of chunked request bodies.

In chunked mode, used when no content length is given, add() holds each chunk in memory until all of it has arrived. A line that is not a chunk-size line, a size line without CRLF, or a size too large to fit an integer leaves the parser waiting forever, and every later add() grows the buffer.

A remote attacker can exhaust memory in applications that pass chunked request bodies to HTTP::Body.

cna.title: @fastify/secure-session vulnerable to signature verification bypass via cookie signature removal

descriptions.value: @fastify/secure-session is a session plugin for Fastify that stores an encrypted session in a cookie. In versions 7.5.0 through 8.4.1, when the plugin is configured with the signed cookie option, it calls the cookie unsign routine but, when the signature check reports the value as invalid, still passes the original cookie value to the session decoder, so a session whose signature did not validate is decrypted anyway. The practical effect appears when an application supplies the cookie signing secret independently of the session encryption key and rotates only the signing secret to retire existing sessions while keeping the encryption key active, because a holder of an old session cookie can strip the now obsolete signature and keep using the session. The attacker must already possess an unexpired encrypted session cookie and needs neither secret, and cannot forge session data, extend expiry, or survive rotation of the encryption key. The issue is fixed in @fastify/secure-session 8.4.2, which no longer decodes the session when the signed cookie option is set and the signature check fails, and users should upgrade to 8.4.2 or later. As a workaround, rotate the session encryption key rather than relying on rotation of the cookie signing secret alone.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-06) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to align query parameter parsing between signature verification and request processing in Keycloak's SAML HTTP-Redirect binding so percent-encoded parameter names cannot evade signature checks: upgrade to the fixed Rhbk/Keycloak Rhel/Keycloak Services builds, which eliminates the parsing discrepancy between raw query parameter signature verification and decoded parameter processing in the SAML redirect binding, closing crafted HTTP GET request containing a percent-encoded unsigned SAML parameter placed before a legitimately signed parameter. Until patched, this is a concern on Keycloak instances configured to use SAML HTTP-Redirect binding for federated identity, so Audit and restrict account registration on external Identity Providers to prevent attackers from capturing legitimately signed redirect-binding messages. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying SAML parameter parsing discrepancy signature bypass — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the SAML HTTP-Redirect binding implementation of Keycloak. The issue occurs because the server processes percent-encoded parameter names (like %53AMLResponse) while the signature verification logic only checks literal parameter names. An attacker can use this discrepancy to provide a crafted, unsigned SAML message that the server processes instead of a legitimately signed one, leading to full account takeover of federated users.

descriptions.value:
Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch vulnerability in deadtrickster ssl_verify_fun allows an adversary in the middle to impersonate a TLS peer via a certificate that carries a partial-label wildcard. try_match_wildcard/4 in src/ssl_verify_hostname.erl anchors only the text before and after the * of an identifier such as f*.example.net, so the wildcard also consumes dots and the certificate is accepted for f.evil.example.net. RFC 6125 confines a wildcard to the left-most label. The same matcher lets *.168.1.1 match the IP literal 192.168.1.1. Whole-label wildcards are matched correctly.

Erlang/OTP 20.0 and later check the hostname in ssl before a user verify_fun sees valid_peer, so a client that keeps server_name_indication set rejects the mismatch regardless. Exposed are clients that disable SNI, servers that verify client certificate hostnames with this library, and direct callers of verify_cert_hostname/2.

This issue affects ssl_verify_fun: from 1.0.1 before 1.1.8.

configurations.value: ssl_verify_fun decides the outcome only where it is the sole hostname check. Erlang/OTP 20.0 and later verify the hostname in ssl before the user verify_fun is called with valid_peer, as long as server_name_indication is a hostname or the connection was upgraded from a socket. A deployment is exposed when it sets {server_name_indication, disable}, when a TLS server uses ssl_verify_hostname:verify_fun/3 to verify client certificates, when it calls ssl_verify_hostname:verify_cert_hostname/2 directly, or when it runs Erlang/OTP older than 20.0. The attacker also needs a certificate with a partial-label wildcard from a CA the client trusts, which the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements do not allow, so the realistic exposure is private PKI.

* Issue a leaf certificate whose only subjectAltName entry is dNSName f*.example.net, for example with public_key:pkix_test_data/1, and decode it with public_key:pkix_decode_cert(Der, otp).
* Call ssl_verify_hostname:verify_cert_hostname(Cert, "foo.example.net"). It returns {valid, "foo.example.net"}, as expected.
* Call ssl_verify_hostname:verify_cert_hostname(Cert, "f.evil.example.net"). It returns {valid, "f.evil.example.net"} although the hostname spans two labels where the wildcard sits.
* Call ssl_verify_hostname:verify_cert_hostname(Cert, "a.b.example.net") as a control. It returns {fail, unable_to_match_altnames}.
* For the IP-literal variant, issue a leaf with dNSName *.168.1.1 and call verify_cert_hostname(Cert, "192.168.1.1"). It returns {valid, "192.168.1.1"}.
* To observe the full TLS path, serve the first certificate from ssl:listen/2 and connect with {verify, verify_peer}, the CA in cacerts, {verify_fun, {fun ssl_verify_hostname:verify_fun/3, [{check_hostname, "f.evil.example.net"}]}} and {server_name_indication, disable}. The handshake succeeds. With {server_name_indication, "f.evil.example.net"} instead, OTP 20.0 or later rejects the certificate with hostname_check_failed before ssl_verify_fun runs.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Identifier parsing. ssl_verify_hostname:try_match_hostname/2 strips trailing dots, tries an exact case-insensitive match, and otherwise calls parse_and_validate_wildcard_identifier/2. That function accepts an identifier with one * in the left-most label and at least two labels after it, and classifies it as SingleCharW when the label is exactly *.

2. Whole-label wildcard, correct. For *.example.net the matcher compares the text after the * with the hostname from its first dot onward, so a.b.example.net fails because .b.example.net differs from .example.net.

3. Partial-label wildcard, incorrect. For f*.example.net the SingleCharW branch is skipped. try_match_wildcard/4 then checks only that the hostname ends with .example.net and starts with f. Nothing checks the span consumed by the *, so f.evil.example.net and f.a.b.example.net pass. RFC 6125 section 6.4.3 limits a wildcard to the left-most label. The wildcard_not_in_a_label/2 guard only rejects internationalized xn-- labels and does not help.

4. IP literals. The reference identifier is treated as a DNS name whatever its shape, so verify_cert_hostname/2 with hostname 192.168.1.1 matches a dNSName of *.168.1.1 through the whole-label branch. RFC 6125 does not apply wildcard matching to IP addresses, and OTP's ssl converts an IP-literal string to an {ip, ...} reference that only matches iPAddress entries.

5. Interaction with Erlang/OTP. When ssl_verify_hostname:verify_fun/3 is used as verify_fun, OTP 20.0 and later call ssl_certificate:validate/4 for valid_peer before the user fun. In the client role with server_name_indication set to a hostname, or with a peer IP from a socket upgrade, OTP runs public_key:pkix_verify_hostname/3 and hands the user fun {bad_cert, hostname_check_failed} instead of valid_peer, which ssl_verify_fun turns into {fail, ...}. OTP's default match function allows no wildcards, and its https match function (public_key:pkix_verify_hostname_match_fun/1) splits both names on dots and matches the wildcard within the first label only. The ssl_verify_fun result therefore decides the outcome only with {server_name_indication, disable}, in the server role, on direct calls to verify_cert_hostname/2, or on OTP older than 20.0.

cna.title: Gitea admin API public-only token scope bypass

references.name: Fix backport to release/v28: go-gitea/gitea pull request #39853

descriptions.value: The `/api/v1/admin` route group did not enforce the `public-only` restriction of personal access tokens. A public-only token with admin scope issued by a site administrator could therefore list private organizations and the email addresses of all users, create organizations, obtain runner registration tokens and create new site administrator accounts, the last of which persists after the token is revoked. Tokens of users who are not site administrators cannot reach these routes; public-only tokens are now rejected on the admin API.

cna.title: Unverified Sign in with Apple callback parameter can override verified ID token claims

descriptions.value: An attacker with any Apple ID can sign in to an application that uses the Apple strategy as any other user whose Apple subject or email they know. Account lookup, account linking, and email-based access control then act on the attacker-chosen identity.

workarounds.value: Remove the user parameter from the callback parameters before you pass them to Assent.Strategy.Apple.callback/2, for example with Map.delete(params, "user"). Without the parameter, decode_user_params/2 yields an empty map and the verified ID token claims pass through unchanged. The user's name is then unavailable, because Apple delivers it only through this parameter.

descriptions.value:
Acceptance of Extraneous Untrusted Data With Trusted Data vulnerability in the Sign in with Apple strategy in pow-auth Assent allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to impersonate another user via the user parameter of the authorization callback.

Apple posts the user's name to the callback endpoint in a user form parameter that the browser submits and the client controls. Assent.Strategy.Apple.callback/2 in lib/assent/strategies/apple.ex decodes that parameter, and fetch_user/2 merges it over the claims of the verified ID token, so the unverified map wins. An attacker who completes a Sign in with Apple login with their own Apple ID and edits the user parameter can replace sub, email, and any other claim. Applications that look up, link, or authorize accounts by the returned subject or email then act on the attacker's values.

This issue affects assent: from 0.1.25 before 0.3.2.

* Start the Sign in with Apple flow of an application that uses Assent.Strategy.Apple.
* Authenticate at Apple with an Apple ID the attacker controls.

2. Authenticate at Apple with an Apple ID the attacker controls.
3. Intercept the `form_post` request to the application's callback URL and set the `user` parameter to a JSON object that carries the victim's values, such as `{"sub": "<victim subject>", "email": "victim@example.com"}`.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Unverified input. Apple's form_post response mode delivers code, id_token, state, and on the first authorization a user parameter that holds a JSON object with the user's name and email. The browser submits this parameter and Apple does not sign it, so the client controls its content.

2. Merge over verified claims. Assent.Strategy.Apple.callback/2 decodes the user parameter with Helpers.decode_json/2 and stores the map in the config under :user. After Assent.Strategy.OIDC.fetch_user/2 has validated the ID token, Assent.Strategy.Apple.fetch_user/2 calls Map.merge/2 with the verified claims first and the decoded parameter second. Keys from the parameter overwrite keys from the token, including sub and email.

3. Result. normalize/2 reads sub and email from the merged map and sets email_verified to true, so the application receives attacker-chosen identity fields marked as verified.

4. Fix. Version 0.3.2 ignores the parameter by default. With include_unverified_name: true, only given_name and family_name are taken from it, and the verified claims are merged over them.

Unverified input.** Apple's `form_post` response mode delivers `code`, `id_token`, `state`, and on the first authorization a `user` parameter that holds a JSON object with the user's name and email. The browser submits this parameter and Apple does not sign it, so the client controls its content.

**2. Merge over verified claims.** `Assent.Strategy.Apple.callback/2` decodes the `user` parameter with `Helpers.decode_json/2` and stores the map in the config under `:user`. After `Assent.Strategy.OIDC.fetch_user/2` has validated the ID token, `Assent.Strategy.Apple.fetch_user/2` calls `Map.merge/2` with the verified claims first and the decoded parameter second. Keys from the parameter overwrite keys from the token, including `sub` and `email`.

**3. Result.** `normalize/2` reads `sub` and `email` from the merged map and sets `email_verified` to true, so the application receives attacker-chosen identity fields marked as verified.

**4. Fix.** Version 0.3.2 ignores the parameter by default. With `include_unverified_name: true`, only `given_name` and `family_name` are taken from it, and the verified claims are merged over them.

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Ahmed Hesham Salah (SecuriCIP) for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: Mitigation for this issue is either not available or the currently available options do not meet the Red Hat Product Security criteria comprising ease of use and deployment, applicability to widespread installation base, or stability.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Pushed Authorization Request PAR implementation of the keycloak-services component. The issue occurs when an authentication flow is restarted, which incorrectly clears the internal markers used to track PAR consumption while leaving the request active. This allows an attacker to reuse the same authorization request to obtain multiple access tokens, bypassing security requirements for single-use requests.

descriptions.value:
Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions vulnerability in the pattern and patternProperties keywords in lud jsv allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass schema validation via a string that matches a schema regex only after heavy backtracking. JSV.Helpers.RegexExt.bounded_match?/2 runs schema regexes with a backtracking budget but calls :re.run/3 without :report_errors, so a match that exhausts the budget returns the same :nomatch as a real non-match. A key that matches a patternProperties regex is then checked against additionalProperties or not at all, and a string that matches a not subschema with a pattern is accepted. Before the budget existed, Regex.match?/2 failed the same way at Erlang's default match limit.

Only schemas whose regex explores a catastrophic branch before the branch that matches are affected. The attacker controls the data, not the schema, and linear patterns never exhaust the budget.

This issue affects jsv: from 0.1.0 before 0.26.2.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* Build a schema with patternProperties mapping the regex ^(?:(a+)+b|a+!)$ to {"type": "integer"}.
* Submit an object whose only key is twenty a characters followed by ! and whose value is the string not an int. The key matches the regex through its second alternative, but PCRE exhausts the 11,050-step budget in the first alternative.
* JSV.validate/2 returns :ok. The value is never checked against the subschema.
* Build a second schema {"not": {"pattern": "^(?:(a+)+b|a+!)$"}} and submit the same string. JSV.validate/2 returns :ok although the string matches the denied pattern.
* Repeat with the short key aaa!. Both schemas now reject the data as expected.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Bounded matching. JSV.Helpers.RegexExt.bounded_match?/2 in lib/jsv/helpers/regex_ext.ex runs each schema regex through :re.run/3 with match_limit and match_limit_recursion set to 10_000 + 50 * byte_size(subject), capped at 10,000,000. The call omits :report_errors, so PCRE's match_limit error is returned as :nomatch. The function compares the result to :match and returns false for a genuine non-match and for an exhausted budget alike.

2. Keyword evaluation. JSV.Vocabulary.V202012.Validation.validate_keyword/3 uses the result for pattern, and JSV.Vocabulary.V202012.Applicator uses it to decide which patternProperties subschemas apply to each key. The draft 7 vocabulary delegates to the same modules. A false from an exhausted budget therefore means a pattern keyword fails and a patternProperties subschema is skipped.

3. Inversion by combinators. Under not, anyOf, oneOf, if and contains, a failing subschema can make the parent succeed, so a false non-match under not accepts a string the deny-list should reject. Under patternProperties the skipped subschema means the value is checked against additionalProperties or nothing.

4. History. Before the budget was introduced, the same keywords called Regex.match?/2, which also returns false on Erlang's default limit of 10,000,000 steps. The budget lowered the input size needed from about 25 bytes to about 20 bytes for the advisory's pattern.

cna.title: Centrifugo: Client-forgeable headers emulation lets any client spoof headers forwarded to proxy backends

descriptions.value: Centrifugo is an open-source scalable real-time messaging server. Prior to 6.9.0, Centrifugo copies the client-controlled protocol.ConnectRequest.headers map through OnClientConnecting in internal/client/handler.go, ConnectEvent.Headers, and SetEmulatedHeadersToContext. The requestHeaders path in internal/proxy/http.go, the requestMetadata path in internal/proxy/grpc.go, and the Consume path in internal/unigrpc/grpc.go can forward an allowlisted value as a trusted backend header or metadata value. A remote client can spoof a header such as x-trusted-user for connect, refresh, subscribe, publish, RPC, and related proxy calls when the backend relies on that header for authentication or authorization. The unidirectional gRPC transport has no transport-level HTTP header that can override the emulated value. This issue is fixed in version 6.9.0.

cna.title: Apache DolphinScheduler: Missing Authorization Checks Allow Non-Admin Users to Retrieve Kubernetes Credentials

descriptions.value:
An authorization vulnerability in Apache DolphinScheduler allows authenticated non-admin users to retrieve Kubernetes configuration data intended for administrator-managed cluster configuration. The exposed kubeconfig data contains credentials that may allow users to authenticate directly to the Kubernetes API outside DolphinScheduler.



The impact depends on the permissions granted to the disclosed credentials. If the kubeconfig provides cluster-admin or broadly privileged service-account access, an attacker may read Kubernetes Secrets, create pods, and establish persistent access to the cluster.



This issue affects Apache DolphinScheduler: from 3.2.0 before 3.4.3.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.4.3, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: Rancher: Ownership-less ClusterRole overwrite via attacker-controlled cr-name annotation on GlobalRole

descriptions.value: CAPEC-176 Configuration/Environment Manipulation
CAPEC-77 Manipulating User-Controlled Variables
CAPEC-240 Resource Injection

A flaw was found in Rancher Manager. The GlobalRole controller derived the target ClusterRole name from the user-settable `authz.management.cattle.io/cr-name` annotation and overwrote that object's rules without verifying ownership. A user with delegated GlobalRole create or update permission could point the annotation at any existing ClusterRole, such as `cluster-admin`, and revoke the permissions of every principal bound to it. The change persists after the malicious GlobalRole is deleted.


This issue affects Rancher: before 2.15.1.

descriptions.value: In OpenStack Designate before 22.0.2, the mDNS handler performs pool-blind lookups when resolving record queries and NOTIFY requests. When two zones with the same name exist across different pools, the lookup fails with a deterministic error, causing the handler to return REFUSED for all DNS queries through that path. The _handle_notify path is exploitable via a single unauthenticated UDP packet. This is independently reachable through the cross-tenant zone overlap described in a different recent CVE, and also affects legitimate same-tenant cross-pool configurations. BIND9 views do not mitigate this issue as mDNS is a shared service upstream of any view configuration.

cna.title: MLS external commit can remove an arbitrary group member

credits.value: Yu Bao from the PayPal Cyber Security Team

affected.vendor: Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc.

descriptions.value: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, validation of an MLS (RFC 9420) external commit's proposal list, org.bouncycastle.mls.protocol.Group.validateExternalCachedProposals, counted the proposals by type and bounded the removed leaf index but never established that the removed leaf had anything to do with the joiner. RFC 9420 sec. 12.2 permits at most one Remove proposal in an external commit, with which the joiner removes an old version of themselves, and requires that where one is present the LeafNode in the commit's path field meet the criteria it would have to meet in an Update for the removed leaf, in particular that its credential present identifiers acceptable for the removed participant. The ordinary proposal-list validator's self-remove rule is deliberately not applied on this path, because a resync commit legitimately removes a leaf the joiner owns, but nothing was put in its place. Any party holding the group's public GroupInfo, which is precisely what an external joiner is meant to be given, could therefore commit a Remove naming any member's LeafIndex and have every member apply it, evicting that member and taking over their slot in the ratchet tree. The credential check that should have prevented this existed only in the gRPC interop harness and so protected no other caller of the public Group.externalJoin and Group.handle API. An external commit carrying a Remove is now accepted only when the removed leaf's credential is identical to the one in the joiner's own new leaf, on both the sending and the receiving side.

descriptions.value: NLTK 3.9.4 through 3.10.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in CrubadanCorpusReader. _load_lang_ngrams joins the corpus root with crubadan_code, the column-0 value read from the corpus table.txt mapping file, and opens the result with the builtin open() rather than the pathsec-validated opener, so os.path.join discards the root when that value is absolute and the read escapes the corpus directory without the containment check nltk.pathsec applies when ENFORCE is set. cna.title: Libkcapi: iv reuse in libkcapi one-shot symmetric cipher chunking causes cipher state reset across chunk boundaries

credits.value: This issue was discovered by Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat.

affected.product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support
Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support

workarounds.value: To mitigate this issue, applications using `libkcapi` should avoid the one-shot symmetric cipher APIs for inputs exceeding 64 KiB when continuous-message semantics are critical. Instead, prefer the streaming interface for processing large messages, or ensure one-shot inputs remain below the internal chunking threshold to guarantee the IV is applied consistently throughout the operation.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in libkcapi. When performing one-shot symmetric cipher operations on large inputs (over 64 KiB) in stateful modes such as Counter (CTR) or Cipher Block Chaining (CBC), the library improperly reuses the Initialization Vector (IV) for each internal data chunk. A remote attacker could potentially exploit this by making an application that uses libkcapi process specially crafted large inputs. This can lead to a significant weakening of data confidentiality, as the repeated IV use can expose relationships in encrypted plaintext, and may also affect data integrity by causing incorrect cryptographic processing.

Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.5 for RHEL 8

Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.5 for RHEL 9
